A massive debris-laden flash flood struck the Budhi Gandaki River in Gorkha's Chumnubri Rural Municipality after a landslide blocked the river flow. Viral footage captured the shocking moment a giant boulder rolled relentlessly down the grey torrent, highlighting the severe destruction caused by the sudden surge. The flash flood swept away more than 35 houses, several bridges, and local infrastructure across riverside settlements like Jagat and surrounding areas. While authorities have reported no human casualties so far, hundreds of residents have been displaced as rescue teams and security forces mobilize to assess the heavy damage. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) and local administration have issued urgent high-risk alerts. Residents along the Budhi Gandaki and Trishuli river corridors have been strictly advised to move away from riverbanks and stay on high ground. For immediate emergency assistance or reporting, contact local disaster management or the Nepal Police hotline at 100 or 112. #GorkhaFlood #BudhigandakiFlood #NepalDisaster #FlashFlood #GorkhaNews

Résultat : des villages rayés de la carte, des routes emportées, des infrastructures entières détruites à la frontière entre le Népal et le Tibet. 🔴 Inundación masiva en Nepal, de nuevo. Una nueva riada golpea este domingo el distrito de Gorkha, en el centro-norte de Nepal. La crecida repentina del río Budhi Gandaki arrasa unas 40 viviendas y varios puentes y deja al menos cinco desaparecidos.El agua también daña instalaciones eléctricas, torres de comunicaciones y las obras de una central hidroeléctrica. El Ejército moviliza helicópteros y equipos terrestres y comunica el rescate de 49 personas. Las autoridades envían unos 200.000 mensajes de alerta para pedir evacuaciones ante el riesgo de nuevas crecidas. Las primeras investigaciones apuntan a un desprendimiento que bloqueó temporalmente un afluente: al romperse la barrera natural, una enorme masa de agua y lodo se precipitó río abajo. Los registros meteorológicos no muestran lluvias en las cabeceras que expliquen la inundación. La emergencia llega cuando Nepal todavía se recupera de las devastadoras inundaciones de agosto, que dejaron más de 1.400 muertos y miles de desaparecidos cerca de la frontera con China. El Gobierno había anunciado esta semana el fin de la búsqueda activa de víctimas de aquella catástrofe para concentrar los recursos en la reconstrucción de las zonas afectadas. 📲 ¡Síguenos para estar al tanto de la actualidad! #inundacion #ultimahora #breaking #nepal #viral

🚨Shocking visuals coming from Nepal's Gorkha District today. A massive, black debris-filled flood surged down the Budhi Gandaki River early this morning after a landslide blocked the river in Chumnubri village. The temporary dam suddenly burst, unleashing a wall of water, mud and rocks. In the video you can see entire buildings with green roofs being swallowed in seconds as people watch helplessly from the hilltop. According to authorities, more than 35-65 houses in Salleri Bazaar, Jagat, Paiyuka and riverbed settlements have been swept away. At least 4 bridges including 2 motorable bridges were destroyed. 5 to 10 people are reported missing so far, and 49 people have been rescued and airlifted by the Nepal Army. A RED ALERT has been issued for downstream districts - Gorkha, Tanahun, Chitwan, Nawalparasi. Residents are being urged to stay away from the river and move to high ground. This comes just 2 months after the deadly August flood in Nepal that killed over 1,400 people. Pray for Nepal. 🙏 #NepalFlood #PrayForNepal #Gorkha #FlashFlood #NepalNews

Nepal has been struck by another major flash flood, this time along the banks of the Budhi Gandaki River in the Gorkha region. The flood wiped out entire neighbourhoods, bridges and damaged a hydropower station. At least five people remain missing. The country is on high alert after a catastrophic flood in August that killed more than 1,400 people, followed by another flood and landslides last month. Nepal is a largely rural nation of 30 million people that has contributed little to the greenhouse gas emissions driving global warming. Its prime minister Balendra Shah says reconstruction could cost billions of dollars. The nation's economy is already under pressure, with limited resources to respond to multiple disasters. Authorities say scores of people in the region left their homes ahead of the Gorkha flash flood, with many now left wondering where they will live.
